messages.text: active checklist problem

I'd love to hear more about this — you mentioned an "active checklist problem." Can you tell me what you're picturing when you say that? And is this something you're bumping into in your own workflow, or something you imagine your clients running into?
Internally

Got it — so this is something happening inside your own practice, not on the client side. When you say "active checklist," what's the thing that isn't working right now? Walk me through a moment where the checklist frustrated you.
I was reviewing overdue checklist and Allison did not complete a checklist from last week - I asked her about it and she said correct I am gonna do it this week

Is this a me problem or should we add a skip this task in the series button with an explanation so if they are not able to complete it when due but the task is reoccurring so they could possible complete it on the next reoccurrence with no problems they can clear the task

Ah, this really clarifies it! So it's not that Allison dropped the ball — the task recurs, and she's just planning to catch it on the next cycle. The 'overdue' flag made it look like a problem when it wasn't. A 'skip this occurrence with an reason' button would let her acknowledge it and move it for, so your overdue review stays meaningful. A couple things I'm curious about: when someone skips, do you still want to see a record of it somewhere, or should it just quietly move to the next occurrence? And is there any case where a skip should NOT be allowed — like a task that truly must get done that period?

I want a record of the skip and the reason why - maybe like with waiting they have to choose a dropdown and an explanation so they could choose themselves, or another colleague or the client. 
I want to be notified each time a skip occurs, and Accountant should be notified if a bookkeeper skips a task assigned to their client.
Maybe a section I can see on my dashboard that shows skipped task this year but once I approve the skip was either legit or a discussion was had it moves out of my dashboard. Like a skip approval process

It should be a quiet skip.
Still available which brings me to where are past completed tasking living currently?

This is the answers to your wrap up questions
It should be a quiet skip.
Still available which brings me to where are past completed tasking living currently?

Perfect — this really pulls it together. So: a quiet quiet skip (no interruption), but they must pick from a dropdown — themselves, a colleague, or the client — plus a written explanation. You get notified on every skip, and accountants get notified when a bookkeeper skips a task for their client client. Skipped tasks land in a skip approval' section on your dashboard, and once you review them (legit or a conversation was had) they clear out. Good question on where completed tasks live now — I don't know your setup, so that's one for you to check: knowing where they go might tell you where skipped tasks should live too. Want me to capture all this in a draft?

Yes, skip should only be on certain circumstances but it could get Grey. Maybe that is a feature when I only set up a task I can choose if it is allowed - if another employee sets up a task I get a notification on the 100% to add if it is acceptable and they do not know it is an option.
Overdue task should be where people see that they have task that are overdue and acknowledge somehow.  Keeping this feature lets me know they are overdue and not being acknowledge and then another talk should happen.

This is great — one more layer I love: skip isn't universal, it's a permission set at task creation. When you build a task you decide if skipping is allowed; when another employee builds one, you get notified so you can add whether it's skippable — quietly, so they don't even know it was an option unless you enable it. And you want to KEEP the overdue view: it's how you spot tasks that are overdue AND unacknowledged, which signals a different kind of conversation. I'll capture all of this now.
For adhoc or one off client time not included in the scope what if we had a button I could push or click to mark it one off time while I reviewed time or something

So when you're reviewing time entries, you'd have a quick button to flag something as 'one-off, out-of-scope work' — that way it's tracked separately from your standard checklist tasks. Are you thinking this helps you see where scope creep is happening, or is it more about just acknowledging the work so it doesn't get lost in the checklist system?
knew idea
. of butdnot theit't but where they DO go now't get done — those show sl't't 'unacknowledged conversation.' Want a separate draratoft this, or fold it it into this same one?
no idea

No idea on what part? Just want to make sure I'm drafting the right thing — are you unsure about something in what we just talked through, or is there a piece of this you want to think more about before I write it up?
for the adhoc idea it would be to help make sure scope creep doesn't happen or get missed I just do not know how the system would be able to track it

Got it — the one-off button is about catching scope creep so out-of-scope work doesn't get missed. The 'how does the system track it' part is genuinely open, and that's okay — it can stay a question for now. Since this feels like a separate thread from the skip idea, I'll write up two drafts so each stays clear. Want me to capture the skip/checklist one first, then the ad-hoc one? For now here's the skip idea — tell me if I've got your words right.

summary: She's seeing overdue checklists flagged as problems when really team members plan to complete them in the next cycle. She wants a 'skip this occurrence' feature with a required dropdown (self, colleague, or client) and written explanation, notifications to her on every skip and to accountants when bookkeepers skip client tasks, and a skip-approval dashboard section she reviews before clearing. Skips should only be allowed on specific tasks—she decides at creation, but gets notified if employees set up tasks so she can approve skip eligibility. She's keeping the overdue view to catch unacknowledged tasks that signal a different conversation. Separately, she wants an ad-hoc button while reviewing time to flag out-of-scope work and catch scope creep, but doesn't yet know how the system would track it—still open.
